britannica.rawText:
TEE                    [ 302 ]                    TEE

TEESDALE, a valley in the north of England.
  TEETH, in anatomy, the hard bodies fixed in the foc-
kets of the jaws, which ſerve to divide and grind the
food. In an adult there are commonly thirty-two teeth,
ſixteen in each jaw; the firſt or milk teeth are twenty
in number, and are ſhed between the ſeventh and the
fourteenth year. Each tooth is covered on its body with
the enamel, which is the hardeſt ſubſtance of the whole
body.
  Toothache ariſes moſt often from a carlous tooth,
when the nerve is laid bare; the vulgar opinion that it
is cauſed by a worm in the tooth has no foundation. The
decay of the teeth proceeds from ſweet things, from
acrid humours of the blood, and from want of cleanli-
neſs; and the teeth ſhould therefore be cleaned daily
with a ſoft bruſh.
  Mr John Hunter has ſhown that a ſound tooth drawn
from one perſon may be tranſplanted into the ſocket of
another, where it often takes root and becomes firm.
The laſt grinders, called dentes ſapientiae, or wiſdom
teeth, appear about the twentieth year, and ſometimes
much later.
  TEETOTUM, a toy.

passages.text: TEETH, in anatomy, the hard bodies fixed in the sockets of the jaws, which serve to divide and grind the food.
In an adult there are commonly thirty-two teeth, sixteen in each jaw; the first or milk teeth are twenty in number, and are shed between the seventh and the fourteenth year.
Each tooth is covered on its body with the enamel, which is the hardest substance of the whole body.
Toothache arises most often from a carious tooth, when the nerve is laid bare; the vulgar opinion that it is caused by a worm in the tooth has no foundation.
The decay of the teeth proceeds from sweet things, from acrid humours of the blood, and from want of cleanliness; and the teeth should therefore be cleaned daily with a soft brush.
Mr John Hunter has shown that a sound tooth drawn from one person may be transplanted into the socket of another, where it often takes root and becomes firm.
The last grinders, called dentes sapientiae, or wisdom teeth, appear about the twentieth year, and sometimes much later.
Humans have two sets of teeth. The primary or baby teeth number 20; the permanent set of an adult numbers 32. The primary teeth are replaced from about age 6 to about age 12.
The crown of a tooth is covered by enamel, the hardest substance in the human body. Below it lies dentin, and the pulp in the centre holds nerves and blood vessels.
Tooth decay is caused by bacteria in dental plaque. They make acid from sugars in food, and the acid dissolves the enamel and dentin.
When decay reaches the pulp, the tooth can become painful and infected.
Brushing the teeth, limiting sugary food and using fluoride help to prevent decay. Fluoride makes the enamel more resistant to acid.
The third molars, or wisdom teeth, usually appear between the ages of about 17 and 25. In some people they never come through.

reasons: Same subject: TEETH and Human tooth.
Rare terms appear in both: enamel, wisdom teeth, thirty-two, twenty.
Tooth decay scores well but covers only part of the entry.

alignments.label: 32 and 20 teeth

britannica.quote: thirty-two teeth, sixteen in each jaw; the first or milk teeth are twenty in number

wikipedia.quote: The primary or baby teeth number 20; the permanent set of an adult numbers 32

alignments.note: The same numbers. Milk teeth are now called primary or baby teeth.

alignments.label: When milk teeth go

britannica.quote: are shed between the seventh and the fourteenth year

wikipedia.quote: replaced from about age 6 to about age 12

alignments.note: The 1797 ages are a little late, but the span is close.

alignments.label: Hardest substance

wikipedia.quote: enamel, the hardest substance in the human body

alignments.label: Worm in the tooth

britannica.quote: the vulgar opinion that it is caused by a worm in the tooth has no foundation

wikipedia.quote: When decay reaches the pulp, the tooth can become painful

alignments.note: The 1797 entry rejected the old tooth worm and blamed decay that reaches the nerve. That view still holds.

alignments.label: Causes of decay

britannica.quote: proceeds from sweet things, from acrid humours of the blood, and from want of cleanliness

wikipedia.quote: They make acid from sugars in food

alignments.note: Sugar and poor cleaning are still causes. Acrid humours are not. Bacteria that make acid were unknown in 1797.

britannica.quote: the teeth should therefore be cleaned daily with a soft brush

wikipedia.quote: Brushing the teeth, limiting sugary food and using fluoride help to prevent decay

alignments.label: Transplanted teeth

britannica.quote: where it often takes root and becomes firm

alignments.note: Hunter did transplant teeth, but most transplants failed and some passed on disease. Wikipedia does not describe the practice.

britannica.quote: appear about the twentieth year, and sometimes much later

wikipedia.quote: usually appear between the ages of about 17 and 25

alignments.label: Fluoride

wikipedia.quote: Fluoride makes the enamel more resistant to acid

alignments.note: Fluoride as a protection against decay was unknown in 1797.

suggestedQuestions: Did the 1797 entry believe in the tooth worm?

Did the 1797 entry believe in the tooth.answer: No. It says toothache comes most often from a carious tooth with the nerve laid bare, and calls the worm a vulgar opinion with no foundation [B4]. Wikipedia says pain comes when decay reaches the pulp [W4].

What causes tooth decay?.answer: The 1797 entry names sweet things, acrid humours of the blood and want of cleanliness [B5]. Wikipedia says bacteria in plaque make acid from sugars, and the acid dissolves the enamel [W3]. Fluoride helps to resist that acid [W5].
